header.notes: sha256 is of the canonical JSON body (JSON.stringify of the file without `header`). Hand-transcribed from the 2026 Form MO-1040ES tax rate chart and instructions; sha256 is of the canonical body. 2026 chart: $0 on the first $1,348 of Missouri taxable income, then 2.0%/2.5%/3.0%/3.5%/4.0%/4.5% in $1,348 steps, 4.7% over $9,436 (matches Tax Foundation 2026). One schedule for all filing statuses; on a combined (joint) return EACH SPOUSE computes tax separately on his or her own share of income using the same chart, so a joint return gets the low brackets twice (worth at most about $180). Standard deduction equals the federal basic standard deduction: 2026 $16,100 single/MFS, $24,150 HoH, $32,200 married filing combined. Filers 65+ or blind also get the federal additional standard deduction ($1,650 each if married, $2,050 if single/HoH in 2026); the married amount is encoded as seniorExtraDeduction. OBBBA deductions (enhanced senior deduction, tips, overtime, car-loan interest) are not allowed. No personal exemption ($1,400 additional exemption for HoH/qualifying widow(er)). Capital gains: H.B. 594 lets individuals subtract 100% of capital gains reported federally (short- and long-term) from 2025 on, so longTermGainExclusionPct is 1 (short-term gains are exempt too). Social Security benefits: fully exempt for recipients age 62+ and SSDI recipients, no income limit (from 2024). Public (federal/state/local government) pensions: exempt up to the maximum Social Security benefit ($47,633 per person on the 2025 return), less any Social Security exemption claimed, no income limit. Private pensions, annuities, IRAs and 401(k) distributions: exemption of up to $6,000 per taxpayer, reduced dollar-for-dollar by Missouri AGI (excluding taxable Social Security) above $25,000 single/HoH, $32,000 married filing combined, $16,000 MFS - i.e. zero for most middle-income retirees. The $6,000 maximum is encoded. Military retirement is fully exempt. Federal income tax deduction: 35% of federal tax if Missouri AGI <= $25,000, 25% to $50,000, 15% to $100,000, 5% to $125,000, 0% above; capped at $5,000 ($10,000 combined) - not modelled. Further 0.1-point reductions of the top rate are contingent on statutory net-general-revenue triggers; 4.7% applies for 2026 per the 2026 MO-1040ES. Brackets are indexed annually for inflation. Not modelled: 1% earnings taxes in Kansas City and St. Louis (wages/self-employment only).

flags.brackets: simplified: on a married-filing-combined return each spouse applies the schedule separately to own income; mfj shown with the single schedule
flags.seniorExtraDeduction: simplified: federal additional standard deduction, $1,650 per married filer 65+; $2,050 if single or head of household
flags.retirementIncomeExclusion: simplified: maximum private pension/IRA/401(k) exemption $6,000 per person, phased out dollar-for-dollar above Missouri AGI $25,000 single / $32,000 married; public pensions are fully exempt
flags.longTermGainExclusionPct: 100% subtraction applies to all federally reported capital gains, short-term included (H.B. 594)
